prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same overly-strict Accept header validation in WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport (src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts, same function around line ~600): the server currently rejects JSON response mode requests unless the Accept header lists BOTH `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`, but per spec a client using JSON-only response mode should be able to send `Accept: application/json` alone. Both PRs modify the identical code block and ship an equivalent changeset description ('allow JSON-only Accept header in streamable JSON response mode'). PR #2204 is unrelated — it fixes a separate bug (treating `parsedBody: null` as no pre-parsed body for AWS Lambda serverless-express compatibility) in a different part of the same file, so it is not part of this cluster. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 introduces a dedicated `acceptsMediaType()` helper that parses the Accept header per RFC 7231 semantics: it splits multiple comma-separated media ranges, reads `q` parameters, and explicitly excludes entries with `q=0` (client signaling it does NOT accept that type). #2046's fix instead replaces the check with a plain `.includes('application/json')` / `.includes('text/event-stream')` substring test, which does not honor `q=0` exclusion or wildcard media ranges (`*/*`, `application/*`) and could misclassify an explicitly-rejected media type as accepted. #1996 implements the more complete, spec-correct version of the same fix.

clusters.pick_reason: #2466 is a smaller, more surgical diff (+114/-4 vs +169/-50) that fixes the root cause directly in StreamableHTTPClientTransport's response handling: it captures Mcp-Session-Id only from successful responses, clears the session on a 404 to the current id, treats 404 as successful termination, and then auto-reinitializes with a fresh session-less InitializeRequest and retries the failed call once. #2150 instead adds a new public transport hook (`onsessionexpired`) on the Transport/Client type that requires the transport to explicitly detect and emit expiry itself, which is a larger surface change and has sat 46 days with no maintainer review. #2466 was opened by a maintainer and is a currently active, unreviewed PR (1 day old) — closing #2150 in favor of it avoids shipping two different public/internal mechanisms for the same session-expiry recovery behavior.

PR #2204 is unrelated — it fixes a separate bug (treating `parsedBody: null` as no pre-parsed body for AWS Lambda serverless-express compatibility) in a different part of the same file, so it is not part of this cluster. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #2466 is a smaller, more surgical diff (+114/-4 vs +169/-50) that fixes the root cause directly in StreamableHTTPClientTransport's response handling: it captures Mcp-Session-Id only from successful responses, clears the session on a 404 to the current id, treats 404 as successful termination, and then auto-reinitializes with a fresh session-less InitializeRequest and retries the failed call once. #2150 instead adds a new public transport hook (`onsessionexpired`) on the Transport/Client type that requires the transport to explicitly detect and emit expiry itself, which is a larger surface change and has sat 46 days with no maintainer review. #2466 was opened by a maintainer and is a currently active, unreviewed PR (1 day old) — closing #2150 in favor of it avoids shipping two different public/internal mechanisms for the same session-expiry recovery behavior.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same line in buildWellKnownPath(), replacing the single-slash strip with the same `replace(/\/+$/, '')` regex — merging both causes a literal conflict. #2215's version (routed through a new normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper) is a superset: it includes the identical multi-slash-strip fix from #2214, but also corrects shouldAttemptFallback()'s root check (`pathname === '/'` -> `pathname === ''`), which never matched after normalization and caused a real extra fallback HTTP request at the root path — a behavioral defect #2214 doesn't address (#2214 is scoped/labeled as a 'chore', #2215 as a 'fix'). Note: #2214 also patches a second, separate inline trailing-slash strip inside buildDiscoveryUrls() that isn't visible in #2215's diff — that hunk should be ported into #2215 during merge to avoid regressing the double-slash case there.
